title: Cross-domain Dependability Activation Manual
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a hands-on activation manual for a coordinated dependability program that spans Serving Runtime, Platform, Console, Product, and Customer Success. It's intended to be pragmatic: a set of lightweight experiments and operational artifacts that let feature teams and SREs converge on meaningful SLOs quickly, validate assumptions, and create repeatable handoffs.

Background/context (short):
- We have fragmented SLIs across model-serving pipelines (hosted API, Dedicated, Private). Teams currently use different latency percentiles, error taxonomies, and tagging.
- Goal: create a short, repeatable activation process to bring a new service from concept -> SLO-backed launch in 6-8 weeks with minimal ceremony.
- This is not the full governance charter. It's an activation playbook focused on field experiments and handoffs.

High-level objectives (what success looks like):
1) Each participating service defines 1–2 primary SLOs with measurable SLIs and agreed error budget policy.
2) Three safety net runbooks (oncall, fallback-to-compatible-model, throttling) exist and have been exercised in a tabletop.
3) Observable signal set and dashboards deployed to Redwood Console: P50, P95, P99 latency, error-rate (by class), token cost per request, queue depth, model-fallback count.
4) Two micro-experiments demonstrate improved cost/latency tradeoffs (batching policy and KV-prefix caching).
5) Clear ownership and handoff checklist completed to move service into steady-state reliability program.

Success metrics (candidate):
- Time-to-first-SLO: median <= 6 weeks for participating services.
- SLO clarity index: all SLOs include target, window, and SLI definition (goal 100% coverage).
- Experiment lift: at least one micro-experiment reduces median p95 latency by 10% or net token cost by 7% for the tested workload.
- Runbook readiness: tabletop exercise executed with oncall and product PMs within 2 weeks of SLO sign-off.

Stakeholders and roles (minimal RACI-style):
- Service Owner (Product/Feature PM): defines user-facing availability/latency expectations, accepts SLO targets.
- Service Engineering Lead: implements SLIs, configures routing/rollouts, partners on experiments.
- SRE Partner: validates SLI instrumentation, builds dashboards, author runbooks, leads tabletop.
- Serving Runtime/Infra: advises on kernel/quantization/instance class decisions for experiments.
- Console/Product Analytics: creates per-route dashboards and cost breakdowns.
- Customer Success & Legal (optional): reviews SLA language for enterprise customers.

Quick activation timeline (6–8 week template):
Week 0: Kickoff (30–60m)
- Attendees: Service Owner, Eng Lead, SRE, Runtime rep, Analytics rep
- Outputs: draft SLO intent, target window, initial SLIs, experiment hypotheses

Week 1–2: Instrument + baseline
- Tasks: implement SLIs, tag requests (model variant, customer tier), capture baseline traffic for 72h.
- Deliverable: baseline dashboard + initial error taxonomy (false positives, timeouts, model-mismatch)

Week 3: SLO proposal + runbook draft
- SRE drafts runbook triggers and escalation tree.
- Service owner signs off SLO intent (target/window).

Week 4–5: Micro-experiments
- Run 2 experiments in staging/prod-dark mode: batching policy tweak, KV prefix cache test.
- Measure impact on latency distribution and cost per 1k tokens.

Week 6: Tabletop + rollback test
- Execute tabletop: simulated incident where fallback-model must be invoked and throttling engaged.
- Confirm runbook actions and time to recovery (TTR) estimates.

Week 7–8: Handoff and steady-state entry
- Finalize dashboards, set alert thresholds, QA automated fallback.
- Handoff checklist completed; service marked as SLO-backed and scheduled for quarterly review.

Micro-experiment design (example templates):
- Experiment A: Dynamic batching window reduction
  Hypothesis: Reducing batching window from 8ms -> 5ms will lower p99 latency for single-request tail without increasing cost > 3%.
  Metric: p99 latency, cost per 1k tokens, throughput.
  Guardrails: rollback if p99 increases by >5% or cost increases >5%.
  Notes: run A/B for 72h during peak traffic window; ensure KV cache warmup is equivalent across cohorts.

- Experiment B: KV-prefix caching for conversation starters
  Hypothesis: Cache common instruction prefixes at edge to reduce KV recompute and overall token generation latency by 8%.
  Metric: mean latency per request, cache hit rate, eviction rate.
  Guardrails: monitor cache saturation and memory pressure; throttle cache population if memory > 70% usage.

Runbooks and triggers (practical snippets):
- Trigger: sustained QPS drop with increase in p95 > 50% for 5m -> Action: scale up instance class (one step), notify SRE bridge, start rollback to previous model variant if degradation persists >10m.
- Trigger: error-rate spike (user visible errors) > 0.5% of requests for 3m -> Action: enable model fallback policy, open incident bridge, route traffic to Dedicated pool if available.
- Trigger: token-cost spike > 30% week-over-week -> Action: throttle low-priority routes, notify cost-ops, start cost-delta postmortem.

Communication plan and rituals:
- Weekly SLO sync (30m): quick health, experiment statuses, decision log. Invite: SRE, Service Eng Lead, Product Owner, Runtime rep.
- Incident retrospective cadence: 72h writeup + 2-week action tracking. Use the reliability experiment board in JIRA.
- Quarterly reliability review: highlight trends, SLO attainment, experiment learnings; decide on policy changes (e.g., acceptable batching windows by service tier).

Decision rules and lightweight governance:
- SLO sign-off requires Service Owner + SRE Partner agreement. If disagreement, escalate to Platform Eng lead.
- Emergency SLO change (customer impacting) must be accompanied by a rollback plan and a postmortem within 7 days.
- Experiments that touch model behavior in prod require a staging A/B run for 72h and an automated rollback switch.

Common risks and mitigations (brainstorm):
- Risk: Teams under-instrument and SLOs become meaningless. Mitigation: SRE provides a minimal SLI template and a validation checklist (scriptable).
- Risk: Experiment noise (traffic shifts) masks impact. Mitigation: run experiments across multiple windows, use traffic-weighted bucketing and synthetic traffic where safe.
- Risk: Runbooks are too long / unreadable. Mitigation: create 1-page action cards with exact commands and escalation contacts.

Lightweight artifacts to create (minimum viable set):
- SLO one-pager (target, window, SLI definition, owner)
- Runbook short-card (3 bullet triage + 1 remediation)
- Dashboard starter template in Redwood Console (copyable JSON id)
- Experiment spec template (hypothesis, metrics, guardrails, rollout plan)
- Handoff checklist (instrumentation | dashboard | runbook | tabletop date)

Notes to self / open questions (raw):
- How do we standardize token-cost attribution per-customer across Dedicated vs Hosted? (auth tag schema?)
- Need a lightweight script to validate that p95/p99 are computed with consistent percentiles and units across telemetry.
- Should we require SLOs for internal-only routes? Maybe a separate "internal" SLO class with different error budgets.

Action items (first sprint):
- [ ] Draft SLO one-pager template (owner: Maya) - due in 4d
- [ ] Create Console dashboard starter and link to seed project (owner: Priya) - due in 8d
- [ ] Build experiment runbook template in GitHub (owner: Carlos) - due in 10d
- [ ] Schedule kickoff with three pilot teams (owner: Ethan) - due in 3d

Appendix: quick links and shorthand references:
- Confluence plan: CONFLUENCE-1234
- SRE experiment board: JIRA-SRE-847
- Template dashboard repo: GITHUB-PR-2201

Endnotes / style notes: keep artifacts short; prefer runbooks that execute in <= 5 commands from bridge notes. This doc is intentionally tactical — we iterate on policy after 2 pilot cycles.
